facts.text: The 'Miracle Pictures' co-producer logo is a gag: no such company exists. Kim Newman says the logo is borrowed from Joe Dante and Allan Arkush's Hollywood Boulevard (1976).
One opening-credits spot has no cast name at all. It reads 'Your Ad Here 555-6748'.
Monique Gabrielle was the role's original inspiration: it was written for her. But producer Roger Corman wanted a TV name, so Teri Copley got the lead and Gabrielle took a supporting part.
Horror legend Forrest J. Ackerman, longtime editor of Famous Monsters of Filmland, cameos as a mortician, holding a copy of his own magazine.
Phantasm's Tall Man, Angus Scrimm, plays the butler Stefen here, spoofing his own famous role. His name is spelled right in the opening credits but 'Angus Scrim' in the end credits.
Uncle Ephram (Jay Robinson) is head librarian at Arkham, a Lovecraft nod. He boasts of 40 years running the world's biggest collection of witchcraft and black-arts books.
Jim Wynorski replaced Charles B. Griffith as director. In 2013 Wynorski said this film 'comes closest to my personality' and 'was the show I never wanted to end'.
Jay Robinson, who plays Uncle Ephram, made his film debut as the scene-stealing Emperor Caligula in the Biblical epic The Robe (1953), and played him again in Demetrius and the Gladiators.
Boris Karloff, dead since 1969, 'appears' via footage lifted from Roger Corman's 1963 film The Terror. Moria reviewer Richard Scheib notes it also supplies reused beach and castle scenes.
Robert Vaughn's Count Byron Orlock shares its name with the Boris Karloff character in Peter Bogdanovich's Targets (1968). Vaughn is best known as Napoleon Solo on The Man from U.N.C.L.E.
Star Robert Vaughn earned an Oscar nomination for The Young Philadelphians (1959) and later played the villain Ross Webster in Superman III (1983).
Hero Dexter Ward and his uncle's workplace, Miskatonic University, are both Lovecraft nods. Dexter Ward comes from Lovecraft's 'The Case of Charles Dexter Ward'.
The film's title comes from a line in the 1962 novelty hit 'Monster Mash'.
Screenwriter Mark Thomas McGee worked on an early draft for about a week before being fired at Roger Corman's request. Corman told director Jim Wynorski he was difficult to work with.
The castle exteriors recycle footage from Roger Corman's Pit and the Pendulum (1961), a shot Corman reused in several films, including The Terror (1963), per Kim Newman.
A scene in 3-D leaves Dexter and Marissa seeing only jumbled red and green, because neither wears 3-D glasses.
Director Jim Wynorski wrote the lyrics to songs 'Just Give Me Action' and 'Think of the Royalties'. Chuck Cirino composed the music.
Howard Morris, who plays Marissa's father, was Ernest T. Bass on The Andy Griffith Show and a Your Show of Shows regular. He also voiced Jetsons characters like Jet Screamer.
Wikipedia says the film's humor is in the vein of Airplane! and Mel Brooks. It also breaks the fourth wall, with one character saying 'I'm in the wrong movie'.
The spell to summon the Evil One includes the nonsense words 'Papa-Oom-Mow-Mow', a pun on the 1962 Rivingtons hit.
Kim Newman notes the plot is borrowed from The Cat and the Canary (heirs searching a castle), with routines lifted from Young Frankenstein. He found the gags 'widely accessible if not very funny.'
The film's credits include a 'Fan of Mr. Vaughn' (Denetia Arellanes) and 'Mr. Wynorski's Favorite Animator' (Kevin Kutchaver).
Besides Monique Gabrielle, scream queens Brinke Stevens, Kelli Maroney and Becky LeBeau appear. Becky LeBeau also sings 'Caught in the Middle of Love'.
Greg Woods of The Eclectic Screening Room argued star Teri Copley showed real comic talent that was never developed, calling this her best big-screen showcase.
Gags include a Pinhead lookalike leaving an acupuncturist's office, and a Phantasm spoof where the silver sphere becomes a baseball.
The $1 million production got a PG rating and few theatrical dates. It was mostly seen on video, even though Monique Gabrielle was famous for nudity elsewhere.
Angus Scrimm, who played Phantasm's Tall Man, won a Grammy as 'Rory Guy' for his 1974 liner notes to a Korngold album.
The Eclectic Screening Room's Greg Woods compared the film's intercutting of classic footage like Boris Karloff's to Dead Men Don't Wear Plaid, and its gag rate to the Marx Brothers.
Wynorski also directed Chopping Mall (1986), and its Ace Mask also plays vampire hunter Victor Von Helsing here. Chopping Mall footage is also listed among this film's connections.
Jay Robinson (Uncle Ephram) made his Broadway debut in 1949's The Shop at Sly Corner opposite Boris Karloff, whose footage is spliced into this film decades later.
Reviews were mixed. Variety praised its 'many delightful reflexive bits'; AMC rated it 1 star out of 5 and TV Guide gave 2.5 out of 4.
Moria's Richard Scheib gave it 2 stars out of 5, calling it 'a serial barrage of lame jokes and bad puns' that is at least painless.
The full soundtrack by Chuck Cirino wasn't released until June 7, 2010, paired with his score for Not of This Earth.
The film's closing credits invite viewers to 'Read The Book of Ulthar. Available soon in paperback.'
Its copyright warning threatens infringers with 'a one-way ticket to Castle Orlock'.
The film was later name-checked in Scream Queen Hot Tub Party (1991) and Invasion of the Scream Queens (1992).
